title: Screeuyn beggey
description: Ten small newspaper columns: a nature diary from a glen with a storm-felled beech, a shore walk with shearwaters and a basking shark, a gardener answering letters after a drought, a Sunday gravy and a fig and banana jelly, a language column on the vocative and irregular verbs, a priest's thoughts on Ash Wednesday, a review of a cyanide murder story, a health column on a cancer lecture and neck pain, a town column on a scheme to demolish an old avenue, and childhood memories of thunder, lace and a balloon.

lessons.title: Yn faih shenn 'sy ghlion
lessons.summary: In his weekly nature column, Leopold Frith describes an early autumn morning in a glen near Laxey: heavy dew on the grass, dim light under the tall conifers, an old beech by the river destroyed by a storm last month but now home to small creatures, a yellowhammer (a bunting) eating berries on an elder, the clear footprints of a badger that sleeps by day, and a tiny shrew, the smallest mammal in the glen, running under the fallen beech.
lessons.text:
Dy chooilley hiaghtin, ta mee screeu screeuyn beg ayns shoh mychione y dooghys ayns Ellan Vannin. Er y hiaghtin shoh, ta mee screeu mychione moghrey ayns glion faggys da Laksaa.

Hie mee magh roish shiaght er y chlag. Va'n soilshey foast dullyr, as va'n aer feayr as glen. Va druight er y faiyr, as va'n druight cho trome as dy row my chassyn fliugh ayns minnid. Tra ta druight trome er y thalloo, ta fys ain dy row yn oie feayr as gyn bodjal.

Ta cassan beg goll sheese dys yn awin. Er y çheu heose jeh'n chassan, ta bearkanee ard. She biljyn bearkanagh ad, as t'ad freayll nyn duillagyn glass ayns y geurey. Fo ny bearkanee, ta'n soilshey dullyr eer ec mean y laa, as cha nel monney lossreeyn elley gaase ayn.

Sheese er oirr yn awin, va faih shenn ny hassoo rish keead blein. Va'n faih shen feer aalin 'sy fouyr, lesh duillagyn doan as buigh. Agh mee er dy henney, haink sterrym mooar harrish yn ellan, as va'n faih stroiet. T'eh ny lhie er y thalloo nish. Va mee trimshagh tra honnick mee eh. Ny yei shen, cha nel faih stroiet ny red marroo son y dooghys. Ta beishtyn beggey cummal ayns y fuygh echey nish.

Faggys da'n faih, ta tramman gaase. She billey beg eh, as ta messyn beggey doo er y tramman 'sy fouyr. Honnick mee pompee buigh er y tramman. Ta'n pompee ny eean beg lesh kione buigh, as t'eh goaill arrane beg aashagh. Ren y pompee ny messyn y ee, as eisht hie eh roish.

Er y thalloo fo'n tramman, honnick mee lorg brock 'sy laagh. Ta brock cummal ayns towl mooar fo'n chronk. Cha vaik mee eh, son ta'n brock cadley 'sy laa as goll magh 'syn oie. Agh va lorg e chassyn feer baghtal.

Eisht, va mee clashtyn red beg ayns ny duillagyn: thollag 'aiyr! She yn sheeintagh sloo 'sy ghlion yn thollag 'aiyr. T'ee cho beg as dy noddagh ee soie ayns laue paitçhey. Ta'n thollag 'aiyr gee dagh oor, er-y-fa dy vel ee cho beg. Ren ee roie trooid y soilshey dullyr harrish yn druight as stiagh fo'n faih stroiet.

Haink mee thie roish nuy er y chlag, as my chassyn fliugh, agh my chree lane.

Leopold Frith

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n traa hie Leopold magh?
Hie eh magh roish shiaght er y chlag.
Cre va er y faiyr?
Va druight trome er y faiyr.
Cre haink er y faih shenn?
Haink sterrym mooar, as va'n faih stroiet.
Cre honnick Leopold er y tramman?
Honnick eh pompee buigh er y tramman.
Cre'n fa nagh vaik eh yn brock?
Er-y-fa dy vel y brock cadley 'sy laa as goll magh 'syn oie.
Cre ta'n thollag 'aiyr?
She yn sheeintagh sloo 'sy ghlion ee.

lessons.title: Er oirr ny marrey
lessons.summary: In her shore column, Araminta Coole writes about a May walk on the coast path for pedestrians south of Port Erin with her daughter Tabitha, who took the photos on the page: the shore is a marginal place between land and sea; Manx shearwaters have come back to the cliffs and to the Calf; a big basking shark with a muscular body swims slowly in the bay but harms nobody; an otter with a long muscular tail comes out of a stream; in a pool by the path there is fish spawn, eggs fertilised in the water and not inside the body; and on the beach Tabitha keeps two smooth egg-shaped stones.
lessons.text:
Ta mee er ve screeu mychione y traie ayns y phabyr-naight shoh rish jeih bleeaney. Ta mee goaill taitnys 'sy traie er-y-fa dy vel ee ny boayl oirragh: cha nel ee thalloo, as cha nel ee mooir. Ta ny beishtyn ta cummal er y traie oirragh myrgeddin. T'ad cummal eddyr daa theihll.

Er y Jesarn, ayns Mee Boaldyn, hie mee as my inneen Tabitha er y chassan coshee sheese veih Purt Çhiarn. She cassan son sleih er cass eh, as cha nel gleashtanyn er. Ta droghad coshee beg harrish strooan ayn neesht. Ta ny jallooyn er y duillag shoh gowit ec Tabitha.

Er y chied çheu jeh'n chassan, ta creggyn ard as y vooir dowin fo. Ayns yn arragh, ta ny scraaylyn çheet erash dys ny creggyn shoh as dys y Cholloo. She eean marrey yn scraayl, doo heose as bane heese. Ta'n scraayl cur un ooh 'sy vlein ayns towl 'sy thalloo. Ta ennym Vannin er y scraayl ayns ny çhengaghyn elley, son ta ram scraaylyn er y Cholloo.

Lurg shen, honnick Tabitha red mooar 'sy vaie: sharkagh! Va'n sharkagh snaue dy moal ec eaghtyr yn ushtey, lesh e veeal foshlit. Ta kirp muskylagh echey, as t'eh ny smoo na baatey beg. Agh cha nel y sharkagh shoh jannoo assee da sleih: cha nel eh gee agh beishtyn feer veggey 'syn ushtey. Ta jallooyn gowit ec Tabitha jeh'n sharkagh, as t'ad feer aalin.

Faggys da'n droghad coshee, ta'n strooan roie sheese dys y vooir. Ayns shen, honnick shin dooarchoo. Va'n dooarchoo snaue 'syn ushtey, as eisht haink eh magh er clagh. Ta kirp liauyr echey, as ta'n famman echey muskylagh. T'eh ymmydey yn famman muskylagh shen son snaue dy tappee. Cha nel dooarchooyn ry-akin dy mennick, as va shin feer vooar jeh.

Ayns poyll beg faggys da'n chassan, va oghyr 'syn ushtey: oohyn beggey ny h-eeastyn. Ta'n eeast cur magh yn oghyr 'syn ushtey, as ta ny oohyn torrit ayns shen. Cha nel ad torrit sthie 'sy chorp, myr ta oohyn ny ein. Tra ta'n oghyr torrit, ta eeastyn beggey çheet magh ass ny oohyn lurg tammylt.

Er y traie, ta ram claghyn oochrooagh, millish as rea liorish ny tonnyn. Ren Tabitha daa chlagh oochrooagh y hroggal, as t'ad nish er y voayrd 'sy chuishlin ain.

Araminta Coole

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Araminta goaill taitnys 'sy traie?
Er-y-fa dy vel y traie ny boayl oirragh, eddyr y thalloo as y vooir.
Cre ta ny jallooyn er y duillag?
Shen jallooyn gowit ec Tabitha, inneen Araminta.
Vel y sharkagh jannoo assee da sleih?
Cha nel. Cha nel eh gee agh beishtyn feer veggey 'syn ushtey.
Cre'n aght ta'n dooarchoo snaue dy tappee?
T'eh ymmydey yn famman muskylagh echey.
C'raad ta oohyn ny h-eeastyn torrit?
T'ad torrit 'syn ushtey, cha nel ad torrit sthie 'sy chorp.
Cre ren Tabitha er y traie?
Ren ee daa chlagh oochrooagh y hroggal.

lessons.title: Lettyryn gys y gareyder
lessons.summary: In his gardening column, Barnaby Thwaite writes that this year there was a long drought in summer and now the first frost has come, with an ice crystal on every leaf, and he has swept the path with a broom; then he answers three readers' letters: Rupert Ainsley in Castletown wants to make a garden of a patch of land full of tall grass and briars and should not use weedkiller, which is harmful, but sow alfalfa to feed the soil; Hester Lumb in Ramsey lost her plants in the drought and should water in the evening; Cuthbert Mayle in Peel has a wet corner and should plant yellow iris, which spreads vegetatively through its roots, though it is harmful to cattle and sheep.
lessons.text:
Ta'n blein shoh er ve aitt 'sy gharey. Va çhirmid liauyr ain 'sy tourey: cha daink fliaghey son shiaghtin er shiaghtin, as va'n thalloo cho creoi as clagh. Nish, ayns Mee Houney, ta'n chied rio er çheet. Er y moghrey shoh, va riojag er dagh duillag 'sy gharey aym. Ta riojag feer aalin 'sy ghrian, agh ta'n riojag jannoo assee da lossreeyn beggey. Lurg shen, ghow mee yn skeab as ren mee ny duillagyn er y chassan y skeabey. Ta skeab mie feer ymmydoil son gareyder 'sy fouyr.

Ta lettyryn çheet hym veih gareyderyn er feie'n ellan, as ta feysht ec dagh gareyder. Shoh three jeu.

Va lettyr veih Rupert Ainsley ayns Balley Chashtal: “Ta preaban beg dy halloo aym cooyl y thie, lane dy faiyr ard as drine. Vod-ym garey y yannoo jeh'n preaban shoh?”

Rupert, foddee oo. Ta thalloo myr shen feer chadjin. Hoshiaght, giare yn faiyr ard as y drine. Ny cur stoo noi lossreeyn er y thalloo: ta'n stoo shen jeeyllagh da ny beishtyn as da'n ushtey. Eisht, cur alfalfey er y preaban. She lus eh yn alfalfey ta cur bee da'n thalloo, as ta fraueyn liauyr echey ta goll sheese dowin. Lurg blein, ver oo yn alfalfey stiagh 'sy thalloo, as bee'n preaban mie son lossreeyn elley.

Va lettyr elley veih Hester Lumb ayns Rhumsaa: “Hooar ny lossreeyn aym baase 'sy çhirmid. Cre nee'm 'sy vlein noa?”

Hester, ta çhirmid er çheet ny s'menkey ayns Mannin. Cur ushtey da ny lossreeyn 'sy fastyr, cha nel ayns mean y laa. Cur duillagyn as faiyr giarit mygeayrt ny lossreeyn, dy reayll yn ushtey 'sy thalloo.

Va'n trass lettyr veih Cuthbert Mayle ayns Pheeil: “Ta boayl fliugh ec bun y gharey aym. Cha nel lus erbee gaase dy mie ayn. Cre nee'm?”

Cuthbert, cur cliogagh buigh ayn! Ta'n cliogagh gaase dy mie ayns thalloo fliugh, as ta blaaghyn buigh aalin echey 'sy tourey. Ta'n cliogagh skeaylley dy losseragh: cha nel eh skeaylley liorish rassyn dy mennick, agh liorish ny fraueyn echey fo'n thalloo. Ta'n aase losseragh shen tappee, as nee'n cliogagh y boayl fliugh y lhieeney ayns blein ny ghaa. Agh freill kiarail: ta'n cliogagh jeeyllagh da ollagh as kirree, my t'ad dy ee eh.

Barnaby Thwaite

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n emshir v'ayn 'sy tourey?
Va çhirmid liauyr ayn, as cha daink fliaghey.
Cre va er dagh duillag er y moghrey shoh?
Va riojag er dagh duillag.
Cre ren Barnaby lesh y skeab?
Ren eh ny duillagyn er y chassan y skeabey.
Cre ta Rupert laccal y yannoo lesh y preaban?
T'eh laccal garey y yannoo jeh'n preaban.
Cre'n fa ta'n alfalfey mie son y preaban?
Er-y-fa dy vel eh cur bee da'n thalloo.
Cre'n aght ta'n cliogagh skeaylley?
T'eh skeaylley dy losseragh, liorish ny fraueyn echey fo'n thalloo.
Vel y cliogagh mie son ollagh?
Cha nel. Ta'n cliogagh jeeyllagh da ollagh as kirree.

lessons.title: Yn aunlyn as y gleihagh
lessons.summary: In her cookery column, Rosamund Pargeter answers the question readers always ask, 'how much?', with a plain Sunday meal: first cleanliness, of the table, the hands and the knife; then a gravy made from the juices of the lamb with flour and water, well mixed with no lumps; a hot dish goes on a mat so it does not mark the table, and her cat sleeps on the mat by the door; and for dessert a jelly with figs and bananas cut with a sharp knife, with a drop of liqueur for the adults but none for the children.
lessons.text:
Ta lhaihderyn screeu hym dy chooilley hiaghtin, as ta'n un feysht oc dy mennick: “Quoid?” Quoid dy flooyr? Quoid dy ushtey? Quoid dy hollan? Er y hiaghtin shoh, ta mee screeu mychione bee aashagh son Jedoonee, as ver-ym dhyt quoid dy chooilley red.

Hoshiaght, glennid. Roish my vel oo goaill toshiaght, glen y boayrd as dty laueyn. Ta glennid ny cuishlin feer scanshoil son bee mie. Ta glennid y skynn scanshoil myrgeddin: glen y skynn lurg dy vel oo er ghiarey feill as roish my vel oo giarey mess.

Son y vee mooar, ta mee aarlaghey eayn. Agh she yn aunlyn yn red share. Tra ta'n eayn aarlit, cur yn ushtey veih'n eayn ayns claare. Cur beggan flooyr ayn, as eisht lieh cappan dy ushtey çheh. Ta aunlyn mie meshtit dy mie, gyn red erbee creoi ayn. Lhig da'n aunlyn ve meshtit son queig minnidyn. Myr shen, bee'n aunlyn millish as blasstal.

Tra ta'n claare çheh, cur eh er breshag er y voayrd. Myr shen, cha jean y claare assee da'n voayrd. Ta breshag elley ayns y chuishlin aym ec y dorrys, as ta'n kayt aym cadley er y vreshag shen dy chooilley laa.

Son y bee millish, ta mee jannoo gleihagh lesh fig as bananey. Gow skynn geyre. Giare three figgyn as daa vananey, as cur ad ayns claare glen. Ta'n fig millish, as ta'n bananey bog. Eisht cur y gleihagh çheh harrish ny messyn, as lhig da'n gleihagh feayraghey son kiare ooryn.

Quoid dy liggar? Son ny sleih aasit, beggan beg dy liggar 'sy gleihagh. Ta blass y liggar mie lesh fig. Agh cha nel liggar erbee son ny paitçhyn! Ta mee jannoo daa gleihagh: fer lesh liggar son ny sleih aasit, as fer gyn liggar son ny paitçhyn.

Rosamund Pargeter

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n feysht ta ny lhaihderyn shirrey dy mennick?
T'ad shirrey “Quoid?”
Cre ta Rosamund gra mychione glennid?
T'ee gra dy vel glennid ny cuishlin feer scanshoil son bee mie.
Cre'n aght ta aunlyn mie?
Ta aunlyn mie meshtit dy mie, gyn red erbee creoi ayn.
Cre'n fa ta Rosamund cur y claare çheh er breshag?
Er-y-fa nagh jean y claare assee da'n voayrd myr shen.
Cre ta Rosamund cur 'sy gleihagh?
T'ee cur fig as bananey 'sy gleihagh.
Vel liggar son ny paitçhyn?
Cha nel. Cha nel liggar erbee son ny paitçhyn.

lessons.title: Lettyr smooinaghtagh mychione grammeydys
lessons.summary: In his language column, Cornelius Ashdown answers a thoughtful letter from Mabel Grundy in Douglas, who is learning Manx: why carrey becomes charrey in 'a charrey' (the vocative form); why the past of faik is honnick (it is an irregular verb, like jean and tar); what the grammarians mean by grooish, a word for a person's look that in grammar is the mood of a verb; and what mygeayrt-y-mooee means ('around her', from mysh and mooee); he adds a note on semantics and on semantic change, says the English words in brackets in her book are useful, and that conversing with people is the only way to learn a language well.
lessons.text:
Hooar mee lettyr smooinaghtagh er y hiaghtin shoh veih Mabel Grundy ayns Doolish. T'ee ynsaghey Gaelg rish blein, as ta feyshtyn eck. Ta lettyryn smooinaghtagh myr shen feer vie, as ta mee booiagh dy reggyrt ad.

Ta'n chied feysht mychione “a charrey”. Cre'n fa ta “carrey” caghlaa gys “charrey”? Mabel, she yn cummey gerrymagh eh. Tra t'ou loayrt rish peiagh jeeragh, t'ou jannoo ymmyd jeh'n chummey gerrymagh: “a charrey”, “a ven”. Ta'n “a” cur er y chied lettyr dy chaghlaa. Ta'n cummey gerrymagh ry-akin dy mennick ayns lettyryn as arraneyn.

Ta'n nah feysht mychione breearyn. Cre'n fa ta “honnick” ayn, as cha nel “faik” ayn? Ta “faik” ny vreear meereiltagh. Ta'n chooid smoo jeh ny breearyn reiltagh: “screeu” as “screeu mee”. Agh ta kuse dy vreearyn meereiltagh ayn, as t'ad feer chadjin: “faik” as “honnick”, “jean” as “ren”, “tar” as “haink”. Bare dhyt ny breearyn meereiltagh shoh y ynsaghey dy mie.

Ta Mabel er lhaih mychione “grooish” ny breearyn. Ta grooish er eddin peiagh: tra t'ou jeeaghyn er grooish peiagh, ta fys ayd my t'eh booiagh ny trimshagh. Ayns grammeydys, ta grooish ec y vreear neesht: t'ee soilshaghey my ta red firrinagh, ny my veagh red er çheet. Ayns “harragh eh”, ta'n grooish soilshaghey nagh vel red shickyr.

Ta'n trass feysht mychione “mygeayrt-y-mooee”. Ta “mooee” çheet veih “mysh”: ta “mysh” son fer, as ta “mooee” son ben. Myr shen, ta “mygeayrt-y-mooee” soilshaghey dy vel red ny lhie ny ny hassoo mygeayrt ben ny inneen. Va'n ven ny soie, as va ny paitçhyn eck mygeayrt-y-mooee.

Ayns lioar Mabel, ta ny fockleyn Baarle ayns lhoobeenyn lurg dagh fockle Gaelg. Ta lhoobeenyn ymmydoil, agh lhaih ny fockleyn Gaelg hoshiaght, as jeeagh er ny lhoobeenyn ec y jerrey.

Ta semantaght ny ayrn jeh çhengoaylleeaght. She studeyrys er keeall ny fockleyn yn semantaght. Ta caghlaa semantagh taghyrt tra ta keeall noa çheet er fockle shenn. Ta Mabel er screeu dy vel caghlaa semantagh doillee dy hoiggal. Ta semantaght ny h-oaylleeaght aitt, as ta ram caghlaaghyn semantagh ry-akin ayns dagh çhengey.

Son jerrey: ta lioaryn grammeydys mie, agh she coloayrt yn ynrickan aght dy ynsaghey çhengey dy mie. Coloayrt rish sleih elley dy mennick, Mabel! Cha nel lioar yn ynrickan red t'ou laccal. Ta possanyn coloayrt ayns Doolish dy chooilley Jerdein.

Cornelius Ashdown

Feyshtyn:
Quoi hug lettyr smooinaghtagh da Cornelius?
Hug Mabel Grundy lettyr smooinaghtagh da.
Cre'n cummey t'ayn ayns “a charrey”?
She yn cummey gerrymagh eh.
Vel “faik” ny vreear reiltagh?
Cha nel. She breear meereiltagh eh.
Cre ta grooish ny breearyn soilshaghey?
T'ee soilshaghey my ta red firrinagh, ny my veagh red er çheet.
Cre ta “mygeayrt-y-mooee” soilshaghey?
T'eh soilshaghey dy vel red mygeayrt ben ny inneen.
Cre'n ynrickan aght dy ynsaghey çhengey dy mie?
She coloayrt rish sleih elley yn ynrickan aght.

lessons.title: Jecrean ny Leoie
lessons.summary: In his faith column, Ambrose Tilley, a priest in Malew, writes about Ash Wednesday: at the altar he puts ashes made from last year's crosses on each forehead, and the ashes remind us of sin, though Lent is a spiritual time and divine love is there for every sinner; he thinks of the martyrs and of a cardinal's red clothes, which recall the blood of martyrs; last Friday he went with a group to the small mosque in Douglas, where people fast by day for a month in the year; the small fraternity in his church helps the poor; and many people today are spiritual seekers, and every seeker is welcome.
lessons.text:
Ta Jecrean ny Leoie çheet er y hiaghtin shoh. She yn chied laa eh jeh ny daeed laa roish y Chaisht.

'Sy cheeill ain ayns Malew, ta mee cur leoie er eddin dagh peiagh ta çheet dys yn altar. Ta'n leoie jeant veih ny crossagyn va ain y vlein shen chaie. Tra ta mee cur y leoie er yn eddin, ta mee gra: “Veih joan haink oo, as gys joan hed oo.” Eisht ta'n peiagh goll erash veih'n altar as soie sheese.

Ta'n leoie cur peccah er cooinaghtyn dooin. Cha nel peiagh erbee gyn peccah, as ta peccaghyn ec dy chooilley pheiagh. Agh cha nel y traa shoh trimshagh ynrican. She traa spyrrydoil eh, traa dy smooinaghtyn as dy ghuee. Ta bea spyrrydoil myr garey: ta feme ayd obbraghey ayn dy chooilley laa. As ta graih jeeoil ayn son dagh peiagh, eer son y fer smoo peccah. Cha nel jerrey erbee er graih jeeoil, as ta'n leoie cur shen er cooinaghtyn dooin neesht.

Er Jecrean ny Leoie, ta mee smooinaghtyn neesht er ny martyryn. She martyr peiagh ta goaill baase son e chredjue. Ta coamrey jiarg er cardinaal 'syn agglish. Ta'n jiarg shen cur fuill ny martyryn er cooinaghtyn: ta'n cardinaal gra dy vel eh aarloo dy gholl baase son e chredjue, myr martyr. Cha nel monney jeu er y theihll, agh ta'n coamrey jiarg oc ry-akin dy aashagh.

Er y Jeheiney chaie, hie mee dys y vosk beg ayns Doolish, lesh possan veih'n cheeill ain. Va failt mie roin 'sy vosk. Ren fer veih'n vosk e chredjue y insh dooin. Cha nel sleih y vosk gee 'sy laa son mee 'sy vlein, myr ta shinyn gee beggan ayns ny daeed laa. Lurg dooin goaill tey, haink mee thie lesh cree lane.

Ta braaraghys beg ayns y cheeill ain: possan dy leih ta cur bee as argid da ny boghtyn. Ta'n braaraghys shoh shenn: va'n chied braaraghys ayns Malew ayns y vlein 1850. Ayns ny daeed laa, ta'n braaraghys çhymsaghey bee as eaddagh son ny boghtyn.

Ta ram sleih nish nyn shirreyderyn. T'ad shirrey bea spyrrydoil, agh cha nel ad goll dys keeill ny mosk. Ta mee gra rish dagh shirreyder: ta failt royd ayns y cheeill ain. She shirreyder dy chooilley pheiagh, er y fa nagh vel fys ain er ooilley, as ta graih jeeoil ayn son dagh shirreyder.

Ambrose Tilley

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Ambrose cur er eddin dagh peiagh ec yn altar?
T'eh cur leoie er eddin dagh peiagh.
Cre ta'n leoie cur er cooinaghtyn dooin?
Ta'n leoie cur peccah er cooinaghtyn dooin.
Cre'n fa ta coamrey jiarg er cardinaal?
Ta'n jiarg cur fuill ny martyryn er cooinaghtyn.
C'raad hie Ambrose er y Jeheiney chaie?
Hie eh dys y vosk beg ayns Doolish.
Cre ta'n braaraghys jannoo?
Ta'n braaraghys cur bee as argid da ny boghtyn.
Cre ta Ambrose gra rish dagh shirreyder?
T'eh gra dy vel failt roish ayns y cheeill.

lessons.title: Lioar noa: Keeaneed 'sy tey
lessons.summary: In her book column, Cressida Holt reviews the new murder story by Ottoline Quarles, whose books have a big cult following: in Douglas in 1925 the tea distributor Thaddeus Crane is found dead in his office with cyanide in his cup, and his worried daughter Sophronia asks the police for help; Peregrine Lusk, who studied psychology in London, finds signs of a short struggle and a letter half destroyed in the fireplace; nothing in the book is random; Lusk's speculative thinking leads him to the murderer, whom Cressida does not name; Quarles also writes speculative stories about the future, but Cressida prefers her murder stories.
lessons.text:
Ta lioar noa ec Ottoline Quarles, as she skeeal marroo eh. Ta cultys mooar mygeayrt ny lioaryn eck. Ta ny lhaihderyn eck çheet cooidjagh ayns Doolish dy chooilley vlein, as t'ad coamrey myr ny persoonyn ayns ny skeealyn. Shen cultys aitt, agh cultys gyn assee.

Ta'n skeeal ayns Doolish ayns y vlein 1925. Ta Thaddeus Crane ny rheynneyder tey: t'eh cur tey veih'n phurt dys dy chooilley happ er yn ellan. Moghrey Jeheiney, ta'n inneen echey, Sophronia, feddyn eh marroo 'sy oik echey. Va keeaneed 'sy chappan tey echey. Ta keeaneed feer jeeyllagh: cha nel feme agh er beggan keeaneed dy varroo dooinney. Ta Sophronia boirit, as t'ee goll dys ny poleenyn.

Ta Peregrine Lusk goaill y chooish. T'eh er studeyrys shicklaage ayns Lunnin, as t'eh credjal dy vel y shicklaage ec y marrooder scanshoil: cre'n fa ren eh eh? Ta Peregrine jeeaghyn er yn oik. Va strepey ayn: ta stoyl er y laare, as ta cappan brisht. Agh cha row y strepey liauyr: ta Peregrine credjal dy row Thaddeus strepey rish y marrooder son minnid ny ghaa ynrican. Ayns yn aile, ta lettyr, agh t'ee lieh-stroiet. Ta beggan fockleyn ry-lhaih foast er y lettyr stroiet.

Cha nel red erbee 'sy lioar shoh gyn tort. Ta dagh red scanshoil: y cappan, y stoyl, eer yn emshir. Ta Sophronia gra nagh row y marroo gyn tort, er-y-fa dy row noid ec yn ayr eck. Ta Sophronia boirit, er-y-fa dy vel aggle urree dy jig y marrooder erash.

Ta Peregrine jannoo smooinaghtyn sheinyssagh: “My ren y marrooder y lettyr y stroie, cre'n fa? Cre va 'sy lettyr? Quoi va'n rheynneyder er screeu huc?” Ta ny smooinaghtyn sheinyssagh shen goll er toshiaght lesh y shicklaage, as ta Peregrine feddyn y marrooder. Cha jean-ym gra quoi eh! Agh va mee lhaih y jerrey ec mean-oie, as va mee boirit son Sophronia!

Ta Ottoline Quarles screeu skeealyn sheinyssagh neesht, mychione y traa ry-heet, as ta cultys ec ny skeealyn shen myrgeddin. Agh ta mee goaill taitnys ny smoo ayns ny skeealyn marroo eck. Ta'n lioar shoh mie, as cha nel eh ro liauyr.

Cressida Holt

Feyshtyn:
Quoi v'ayn Thaddeus Crane?
V'eh ny rheynneyder tey ayns Doolish.
Cre va 'sy chappan tey echey?
Va keeaneed 'sy chappan tey echey.
Cre'n fa ta Sophronia boirit?
Ta aggle urree dy jig y marrooder erash.
Cre ren Peregrine Lusk y studeyrys ayns Lunnin?
Ren eh shicklaage y studeyrys.
Cre hooar Peregrine 'syn aile?
Hooar eh lettyr lieh-stroiet 'syn aile.
Vel red erbee 'sy lioar gyn tort?
Cha nel. Ta dagh red 'sy lioar scanshoil.

lessons.title: Toyrt mychione kahngyr
lessons.summary: In her health column, Lucinda Marsh writes about an academic presentation in Douglas by Ignatius Pell, a lecturer in biology who studies cancer: cells duplicate themselves when the body needs them, but in cancer the duplicating does not stop and can speed up, so a doctor should not be hasty but should not wait either; the people in the hall, Lucinda too, were held by fascination; then she answers Dorcas Penrose, who has neck pain every morning when she gets out of bed: her bed may be too soft, she should not look down at her phone for hours, and she should not get up from bed in a hurry.
lessons.text:
Er y Jerdein, hie mee dys toyrt ollooagh ayns Doolish. Va'n toyrt ec Ignatius Pell, leaghteyr ayns bea-oaylleeaght. Ta'n leaghteyr shoh gobbraghey mychione kahngyr rish feed blein. Cha nel toyrt ollooagh aashagh dy hoiggal dy mennick, agh va'n toyrt shoh baghtal as aashagh.

Ta kirp dooinney lane dy chillagyn. Ta ny killagyn dooblaghey ad hene: ta un chillag goll dy ve daa chillag. Ayns kirp slane, ta'n dooblaghey shoh reiltagh, as t'eh taghyrt tra ta feme er ynrican. Agh ayns kahngyr, cha nel y dooblaghey scuirr. Ta ny killagyn dooblaghey ad hene reesht as reesht. Dooyrt y leaghteyr dy vod y dooblaghey siyraghey: ta'n kahngyr gaase dy moal hoshiaght, as eisht ta'n aase siyraghey. Er-y-fa shen, cha lhisagh shin ve siyragh, agh cha lhisagh shin fuirree ro liauyr neesht.

Va drualtys er ny sleih 'sy halley. Va drualtys orrym hene neesht. Va jallooyn ec y leaghteyr jeh killagyn kahngyr, as v'ad aalin, ga dy vel ad jeeyllagh. Lurg y toyrt, va feyshtyn ec ram sleih, as ren y leaghteyr freggyrt dagh feysht. Va'n toyrt ollooagh shoh yn toyrt share honnick mee rieau.

Hooar mee lettyr er y hiaghtin shoh veih Dorcas Penrose: “Ta pian mhuinneelagh orrym dy chooilley voghrey tra ta mee irree veih'n lhiabbee. Cre nee'm?”

Dorcas, ta pian mhuinneelagh feer chadjin. Hoshiaght, jeeagh er dty lhiabbee. My ta'n lhiabbee ro vog, cha nel y mwannal ayd jeeragh car ny h-oie. Bare lhiam lhiabbee ta beggan creoi. Nish, jeeagh er dty laghyn. Vel oo jeeaghyn sheese er dty çhellvane son ooryn? Ta ram sleih çheet dys my oik lesh pian mhuinneelagh er y fa shen. Cur y çhellvane ny s'yrjey, as jeeagh jeeragh er.

As son jerrey: ny bee siyragh 'sy voghrey. Ny irree veih'n lhiabbee dy siyragh. Lhie er dty lhiabbee son minnid, eisht soie, as eisht irree. My ta'n pian ayn foast lurg shiaghtin ny ghaa, tar dys my oik.

Lucinda Marsh

Feyshtyn:
Quoi v'ayn Ignatius Pell?
V'eh ny leaghteyr ayns bea-oaylleeaght, as t'eh gobbraghey mychione kahngyr.
Cre ta ny killagyn jannoo ayns kahngyr?
T'ad dooblaghey ad hene reesht as reesht, gyn scuirr.
Row drualtys er ny sleih 'sy halley?
Va. Va drualtys orroo ooilley, as er Lucinda neesht.
Cre'n pian t'er Dorcas?
Ta pian mhuinneelagh urree dy chooilley voghrey.
Cre'n fa nagh vel y mwannal jeeragh car ny h-oie?
Er-y-fa dy vel y lhiabbee ro vog.
Cre ta Lucinda gra mychione y voghrey?
T'ee gra rish Dorcas nagh lhisagh ee ve siyragh 'sy voghrey.

lessons.title: Yn astyl as y skeym noa
lessons.summary: In his town column, Montague Riddle writes that the council in Douglas has a new scheme to demolish the old houses on the tree-lined avenue behind the harbour to make a wide road for traffic, which is heavy, with cars and motorbikes, above all at the motorbike races in June; the houses were built in 1840 under the patronage of a merchant whose name is cut in stone at the end of the avenue; at a public forum last Wednesday many people said the houses should not be demolished; an old map from 1834, made by an engraver on metal, shows the journey from the harbour to the church as a path through fields, and Montague praises the craft of cartography; after the forum he made that journey on foot.
lessons.text:
Ta skeym noa ec y choonseil ayns Doolish. T'ad laccal ny shenn thieyn er yn astyl cooyl y phurt y lhieggey, dy yannoo raad lhean son traghtey. Ta ram traghtey ayns Doolish, er-y-fa dy vel ny gleashtanyn as ny roaryn-bree goll trooid y valley dy chooilley laa. Ayns Mean Souree, tra ta ratçhal roar-bree ayn er yn ellan, ta'n traghtey roar-bree feer vooar. Ta'n skeym shoh er ve ayns ny pabyryn-naight rish mee.

Agh ta'n astyl shoh aalin. Ta biljyn er dagh çheu jeh'n astyl, as ta thieyn shenn veih'n vlein 1840 ayn. Va ny thieyn troggit fo patroonys fer-dellal lesh ram argid, as ta'n ennym echey grainnit er clagh ec kione yn astyl. Va'n patroonys echey mooar: hug eh argid son y cheeill as son y scoill neesht. Gyn y patroonys echey, cha beagh yn astyl ayn.

Hie mee dys y forym er y Jemayrt chaie. Va'n forym ayns halley y valley, as va keead peiagh ayn. Dooyrt fer veih'n choonseil dy vel y traghtey ro vooar son ny raaidyn beggey. Agh dooyrt ram sleih 'sy forym nagh lhisagh y coonseil ny thieyn y lhieggey. “Lurg dhyt thie shenn y lhieggey, cha jig eh erash,” dooyrt ben aeg.

Va kaart shenn ec y forym. Va'n kaart jeant 'sy vlein 1834. Ren grainneyder y kaart er meain, as eisht v'eh prentit er pabyr. Ta ennym y grainneyder screeuit er oirr y chaart. Ta kaartgraafeeaght ny cheird aalin: ta feme er y fer ta jannoo kaart dy ve kiart, as ta feme echey er laue vie. Ta ram ry-ynsaghey mychione kaartgraafeeaght veih kaart myr shen, as ta mee credjal dy vel kaartgraafeeaght ny h-ellyn myrgeddin.

Ta'n kaart soilshaghey yn troailtys veih'n phurt gys y cheeill ec y traa shen: cassan beg trooid magheryn. Nish, ta'n troailtys shen jeant ayns gleashtan ayns queig minnidyn. Lurg y forym, ren mee yn troailtys shen er cass, as ren mee shassoo ec kione yn astyl son tammylt.

Cha nel fys ain foast cre nee'n coonseil. Bee forym elley ayn 'sy vee noa, as bee mee ayn.

Montague Riddle

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n skeym t'ec y choonseil?
T'ad laccal ny shenn thieyn er yn astyl y lhieggey.
Cre'n fa ta'n coonseil laccal raad lhean?
Er-y-fa dy vel ram traghtey ayns Doolish.
Fo patroonys quoi va ny thieyn troggit?
V'ad troggit fo patroonys fer-dellal lesh ram argid.
C'raad va'n forym?
Va'n forym ayns halley y valley.
Quoi ren y kaart shenn?
Ren grainneyder y kaart er meain.
Cre ren Montague lurg y forym?
Ren eh yn troailtys veih'n phurt gys y cheeill er cass.

lessons.title: Cooinaghtyn veih my lambaanid
lessons.summary: In her column, Winifred Ashby writes about her childhood after a visit to the Manx Museum in Douglas, where a new room shows toys from the 1960s as artefacts, among them a small red percussion instrument like the one she had; she remembers her grandmother's house in Ramsey, with a white lace cloth on the table and a crystal dish she was not allowed to touch; she was afraid of thunder until her grandfather made a joke that the clouds were playing their drum; and at the beach a seller of balloons gave her a second balloon for nothing when the wind took the first; now her childhood is an artefact in a museum, and she is glad.
lessons.text:
Ta mee er ve smooinaghtyn mychione my lambaanid er y hiaghtin shoh. Hie mee dys Thie Tashtee Vannin ayns Doolish, as honnick mee jeantaneyn shenn ayns shamyr noa: greieyn cloie veih ny bleeantyn 1960. Va ennym as blein screeuit ec dagh jeantane. Ayns ny jeantaneyn shen, honnick mee my lambaanid hene.

Va greie bwoallee beg jiarg ayn. She greie bwoallee eh ta paitçhyn bwoailley lesh nyn laueyn. Va greie bwoallee myr shen aym tra va mee shey bleeaney d'eash, as va mee bwoailley eh dy chooilley laa. Cha row my voir booiagh lesh y sheean!

Ayns my lambaanid, va mee goll dys thie my shenn-voir ayns Rhumsaa dy chooilley hourey. Va eaddagh laatçhey bane er y boayrd eck. Va'n laatçhey shen jeant ec moir my shenn-voir, as v'eh feer aalin. Er yn eaddagh laatçhey, va claare crystallagh, as messyn ayn. Cha row kied aym laue y chur er y chlaare crystallagh. “Ta'n claare crystallagh shoh shenn,” dooyrt my shenn-voir. “Cha nod oo cloie lesh.”

Va aggle orrym roish taarnagh. Tra va taarnagh ayn, va mee follaghey fo'n voayrd. Oie dy row taarnagh trome ayn, ren my shenn-ayr spotçh: “Ta ny bodjallyn cloie lesh y greie bwoallee oc!” Ren mee gearey, as cha row aggle orrym roish taarnagh ny sodjey. V'eh cur spotçh er dagh nhee, my shenn-ayr. Cha row dagh spotçh echey mie, agh va shin gearey ec ooilley.

Ayns y tourey, va creckeyder ec y traie ayns Rhumsaa, as va balloon jiarg ec y creckeyder son dagh paitçhey. Hug my shenn-ayr argid da'n chreckeyder, as hooar mee balloon. Agh ren y geay y balloon y ghoaill, as hie eh seose 'syn aer. Va mee keayney. Ren y creckeyder balloon elley y chur dou, gyn argid.

Nish, ta my lambaanid ny jeantane ayns thie tashtee! Agh ta mee booiagh. Ta ny cooinaghtyn shoh sauail ayns shen, son paitçhyn noa.

Winifred Ashby

Feyshtyn:
Cre honnick Winifred ayns y thie tashtee?
Honnick ee jeantaneyn shenn: greieyn cloie veih ny bleeantyn 1960.
Cre va er y boayrd ec y shenn-voir eck?
Va eaddagh laatçhey bane er y boayrd, as claare crystallagh.
Row kied ec Winifred cloie lesh y claare crystallagh?
Cha row. Va'n claare crystallagh shenn.
Cre'n spotçh ren y shenn-ayr eck?
Dooyrt eh dy row ny bodjallyn cloie lesh y greie bwoallee oc.
Cre ren y creckeyder tra hie yn chied balloon seose 'syn aer?
Ren eh balloon elley y chur da Winifred, gyn argid.
